questions.question: Describe how to set up and keep a weather diary.
questions.expected_answer: Make a table with columns for the date and time, temperature in degrees Celsius, cloud cover, precipitation type and amount in millimetres, wind direction and strength, and comments. Observe at the same times every day with the same instruments in the same places, write readings down straight away, and leave a missed reading empty with a reason instead of guessing.

questions.question: How can graphs help you find weather patterns?
questions.expected_answer: A line graph shows temperature going up and down over the days, and a bar graph shows how much rain fell each day. Graphs make patterns easy to see, such as afternoons being warmer than mornings, colder mornings after clear nights, and cooler weather after a storm.

questions.question: Give an example of a good comment on how weather affected daily life.
questions.expected_answer: A good comment links the weather to its effect and explains why, for example: on Tuesday the wind was strong from the north-west, so the air was full of dust and we stayed inside at break. Another example: the thunderstorm caused a power cut, but it watered the vegetable garden.
